verses.text: Jesus began teaching beside the sea. The crowd around him got so huge that he climbed into a boat and sat out on the water, while everyone stayed on shore.
He taught them many things through parables. Here’s how he taught:
“Listen up! A farmer went out to scatter seed.
“As he scattered it, some seed fell beside the road. Birds came and ate it up.
“Some fell on rocky ground, where there wasn’t much soil. It sprouted fast because the soil was shallow.
“But when the sun came up, it got scorched. With no roots, it dried up.
“Some seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew and choked it, so it produced nothing.
“Some landed in good soil and grew, producing a crop: thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times what was planted.” 🌱
Then Jesus said, “If you have ears to hear, listen!”
When Jesus was alone, the people around him, along with the twelve, asked him about the parables.
He told them, “You’ve been given the secret of God’s Kingdom. For the people outside, everything comes through parables,
“so they may look and look but not see, hear and hear but not understand; otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven.”
Then Jesus asked them, “You don’t understand this parable? How will you understand any of them?
“The farmer scatters God’s message.
“Some people are like seed beside the road, where the message lands. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and snatches the message away.
“Others are like seed on rocky ground. They hear the message and welcome it right away, all excited.
“But they have no roots, so they don’t last. When trouble or persecution comes because of the message, they trip up immediately.
“Others are like seed among thorns. They hear the message,
“but worries about this age, the trickiness of wealth, and all kinds of other desires crowd in and choke it. The message produces nothing.
“And some are like seed in good soil. They hear the message, welcome it, and produce a crop—thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times what was planted.”
Jesus also said, “Do you bring in a lamp just to hide it under a basket or a bed? No—you put it on a stand.
“Nothing is hidden unless it’s meant to be revealed; nothing is kept secret except so it can come out into the open.
“If you have ears to hear, listen!”
Then he told them, “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be used for you—and more will be added.
“Whoever has something will be given more; whoever has nothing will lose even what they have.”
Jesus said, “God’s Kingdom is like someone scattering seed on the ground.
“He goes to sleep at night and gets up in the morning. The seed sprouts and grows, though he doesn’t know how.
“The earth produces the crop on its own: first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
“Once the grain is ready, he sends in the sickle, because harvest time has come.” 🌾
Jesus also asked, “What can we compare God’s Kingdom to? What story can help us get it?
“It’s like a mustard seed. When it’s planted in the ground, it’s the smallest of all the seeds there.
“But once it’s planted, it grows and becomes the biggest garden plant, with branches so large that birds can nest in its shade.”
Jesus used many parables like these to share God’s message, as much as the people were able to understand.
He didn’t teach them without a parable. But when he was alone with his disciples, he explained everything to them.
That same day, when evening came, Jesus said to them, “Let’s cross over to the other side.”
They left the crowd and took Jesus with them in the boat, just as he was. Other boats came along too.
A fierce windstorm sprang up, and waves crashed into the boat until it was filling with water.
Jesus was in the back of the boat, asleep on a cushion. They woke him: “Teacher, do you even care that we’re about to die?”
He got up, ordered the wind to stop, and told the sea, “Quiet! Be still!” The wind died down, and everything went completely calm.
Jesus said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Don’t you have faith yet?”
They were overwhelmed with fear and said to one another, “Who is this? Even the wind and the sea obey him!”
